title: Lagged four-week Federal Reserve balance-sheet growth DRA V1 entry admission
thesis: A positive four-week change in the Federal Reserve's weekly total assets may identify an expanding broad-liquidity state in which unchanged long DRA momentum entries have better realized breadth and inventory paths. Vetoing new parent entries during non-expansion may improve equal-capital DRA economics without altering exits or existing lots.
mechanism: For weekly Wednesday WALCL observation D, compare the level with the exact observation 28 calendar days earlier. Beginning at D plus three calendar days 00:00 UTC and for at most 168 hours, admit an otherwise unchanged DRA V1 parent signal only when the change is strictly positive; otherwise veto the new entry and leave all existing lots and exits untouched.
economic_rationale: The feature is useful only if it improves both Design and Validation total and realized PnL, preserves unrealized PnL, drawdown, underwater duration, holding and terminal inventory, intervenes often enough, and has annual and predictive breadth. A COVID-era gain, fewer trades, current-vintage correlation or terminal inventory cleanup is insufficient.
